b = Node("b", Node("c", Node("d")), Node("e", Node("f")))
tree_diameter(Node("a", b))
start: Draw `a` with a single child `b`, and give `b` two branches: `c` then `d` on the left, `e` then `f` on the right. The longest path runs from `d` up through `b` and down to `f`, four edges, and never touches `a`. Every path has one highest node, where it turns from going up to going down.

Postorder: finish both children before their parent. Each node hands its parent one number, its height (nodes on its longest downward branch, 0 for a missing child), and since a parent can extend only one branch, that is `1 + max(left, right)`. The longest path turning at the node has `left + right` edges: keep the best of those over every node, separately.

start.text: The tests use a 5,000-node chain, so use an explicit stack and put each node on it twice: once to push its children, and once, when their heights are known, to combine them. The shape:

test_units_and_deep_chain: `None` and a single node both give `0`: the answer counts edges, not nodes. The README's tree gives `3`, from `d` or `e` up through `b` and `a` to `c`. Then a 5,000-node chain of `left` children must give `4999`, and a recursive walk stops at Python's recursion limit of about 1,000 calls long before that.

The last check hangs the longest path below the root: the root's only child has two branches of three nodes each, answer `6`. The root's own `left + right` is only `4`, so keep the best `left + right` over every node.
test_invalid_structure: A node whose `left` is itself, a node whose two children are the same object, a node whose `right` is `42`, and `42` as the root must each raise `ValueError`. Check `isinstance(node, Node)` on every node you step onto, and keep a set of the nodes you have entered: meeting one twice means a loop or a shared child.
test_all_pairs_distance_oracle: 150 random trees of 1 to 29 nodes, checked against a breadth-first search from every node that keeps the farthest distance, so the path may start and end anywhere. An answer off by one or two usually mixes units: heights that count nodes, with a missing child at 0, give a path of exactly `left + right` edges.

RecursionError: “Units and deep chain” builds a 5,000-node chain, and Python stops recursion at about 1,000 calls. Use an explicit stack and handle each node twice: once to push its children, once to combine their heights.
In “Invalid structure” it can mean a walk went round the node whose `left` is itself. Keep a set of the nodes you have entered and raise `ValueError` on a repeat.
AttributeError: You read `.left` or `.right` on `42`, the right child and the root in “Invalid structure”. Check `isinstance(node, Node)` before reading a node's children, and raise `ValueError`.
KeyError: Reading a child's height with `height[node.left]` fails when that child is missing, since `None` never got a height. A missing child has height `0`: read it with `.get(child, 0)`.

stopped: A stack loop that never ends is going round the node whose `left` is itself, in “Invalid structure”. Keep a set of the nodes you have entered, and raise `ValueError` on a repeat before pushing its children.
If each node goes on the stack twice, the second push must be marked as done. A frame that pushes its children every time it comes off the stack refills the stack forever.
passing: All passing. Time a chain of 100,000 nodes as your own input next to one of 50,000: it should take about twice as long, since each node is entered once and finished once. Then the README's first follow-up: what else must each node return so you can name the two end nodes of the longest path?
